1. Cost of services: Probably the biggest upside is that for relatively little money, you can be a big shot. The cost of labor will be so low that you can easily hire, for a few dollars, a private driver for the day. In places like Vietnam, if you want a new suit, grab a photo of what you want and head down to the tailor district. $150 later you'll have a perfectly tailored silk or wool suit that has the workmanship and quality of what you would pay $5000 for in the States. Restaurant meals and alcohol will be much cheaper in comparison, too. Note that the flipside of this, however, is that you have to quite vigilant against being taken advantage of, especially when you don't speak the language. If someone just straight up steals your stuff while working on your car, for example, expect no help whatsoever from the police.

  2. Things are just more ... interesting. If you visit a third world country and have a few beers from a patio overlooking the city center, it's just a theater of humanity you don't get in developing countries. Children driving pickups, dogs meandering the streets, people dancing in the streets, etc. It might sound voyeuristic, and maybe it is, but people watching is just a whole new thing.

  3. Bribery is a thing in most third world countries, which is strictly speaking a downside; no one wants to live in an economy where bribery is rampant. Note that there are exceptions. Cuba is a third world country, but you most certainly cannot bribe the police. Chile is another example of a second world country where trying to payoff the police is a very bad idea. But in most of Africa, South America, and much of developing Asia, the police take (and expect) bribes. While this means that you have to always carry a small amount of cash, it also means you can get away with small crimes. Did you get a little too shitfaced at the bar? $100 and the officer will probably look the other way.

Food, hands down. Chances are anything you get is coming from the 50 mile radius and not coming off an assembly line because it just isn't affordable to do it that way. Of course you'll want to ease in to it if your gullet isn't used to the 'gullet-flora' of the area ;)
